records.title: Pyrrolizidine Alkaloids in Tea and Dietary Exposure Assessment of Tea Intake
records.source_title: Pyrrolizidine Alkaloids in Tea and Dietary Exposure Assessment of Tea Intake
records.abstract: Investigators used HPLC-MS/MS to measure pyrrolizidine alkaloids and their N-oxides in 63 tea samples from several processing categories. They detected at least one monitored compound in 77.78 percent of samples, with a mean reported level of 17.67 micrograms per kilogram. A margin-of-exposure and Monte Carlo analysis modeled possible dietary risk under assumptions about consumption. These are product-level analytical and simulated exposure findings, not observed liver injury or direct evidence about individual consumers.
records.relevance_reason: Direct primary analytical evidence of botanical product contaminants with clear limits on risk interpretation.
records.study_design: Cross-sectional product sampling and modeled dietary exposure

study_details.method: HPLC-MS/MS and Monte Carlo exposure modeling

records.population: 63 commercial tea samples; simulated consumer exposures
records.intervention: Analytical screening of tea for pyrrolizidine alkaloids and N-oxides
records.comparator: Tea-processing categories and simulated consumption scenarios
outcomes: 77.78 percent of samples had a detected analyte
Mean detected concentration reported as 17.67 micrograms per kilogram
records.uncertainty: Sampling and modeled intake assumptions limit extrapolation to real-world individual health outcomes.
records.adverse_effects: Potential toxicological exposure hazard, without clinical adverse events observed in this study.
records.limitations: Small product sample; modeled exposure instead of prospective human health outcomes.
